children: South Korea is set to post another month of solid chip-led export growth for August, with its trade surplus expected to top $30 billion for a third straight month. The median forecast from a Wall Street Journal poll of 13 economists is for a 62.0% on-year increase in shipments overseas, following a revised 63.0% rise in July. Imports are projected to have risen 22.4% on year, resulting in a $30.39 billion trade surplus in August. Overall export growth was likely driven by semiconductors and other IT products, while automobile exports stayed sluggish amid labor strikes in the sector, says iM Securities' Park Sang-hyun. The trade data are due Tuesday.(kwanwoo.jun@wsj.com)
